  • 避開費用陷阱：深入揭露 Claude 各模型與思考預算設定中「花費更高卻未必更好」的直覺誤區。
  • 多維度極限實測：透過無網路 3D 物理動態、精密機械連動與長文本空間組裝三大嚴苛任務，全方位檢驗真實代碼能力。
  • 性價比指南：提供詳細的時間、API 成本與生成細節對比，協助開發者依據實際場景選出最具成本效益的模型配置。

摘要

模型選擇的迷思與實測背景

作者指出，許多人在面對 Anthropic 的 Claude 系列模型及思考預算切換開關時，往往會依照直覺挑選，但這些選擇背後卻暗藏成本翻倍或性能不符預期的陷阱。例如使用輕量級模型進行多輪編程時可能觸發高倍費率，或開啟最高智慧等級卻多付了將近兩成費用且未帶來明顯效益。為了釐清真相，作者針對多種配置與模式展開了相同條件下的橫向評測，從生成品質、耗費時間與API 成本進行深度剖析。

第一輪測試：3D 越野車越障模擬

第一項挑戰要求模型在完全斷網的環境下，撰寫出能夠翻越 18 公分減速帶的3D 越野車動力模擬。雖然所有配置皆成功運行，但在細節呈現上差距甚大。高階配置成功還原了雨後地面積水倒影、乾淨車窗以及與實車相同的並列彈簧避震結構；官方預設模式則以最快速度與適中成本取得極佳平衡。相對地，低階模型不僅材質簡陋，甚至出現了煞車卡鉗隨輪胎轉動的荒謬機械錯誤。

第二輪測試：精細機械蝴蝶與展開視圖

第二項測試聚焦於多層微型零件聯動，要求模型打造出兼具金屬鏤空、彩繪玻璃與胸腔齒輪聯動的互動式 3D 機械蝴蝶，並支援一鍵爆炸圖拆解。在此測試中，中低階模型紛紛暴露出過曝、透明度欠佳或結構如玩具般的缺陷。兩款頂級配置在細節與節奏感上難分伯仲，但作者特別指出，開啟最高思考預算的模式耗時與費用足足翻倍，肉眼可見的成果卻無實質差距。

第三輪測試：長文本空間組裝導引

第三輪任務考驗長文本理解與空間幾何組裝，模型需依據五頁英文家具手冊，將 32 個板材零件按孔位和順序轉化為互動組裝流程。這項測試徹底拉開了高低階之間的差距：低階模型組裝邏輯完全崩潰、桌面漂浮空中；中階模型能流暢運行卻遺漏了凹槽等細部特徵；唯有頂規配置能精準定位零件輪廓並嵌入手冊圖解，展現出處理複雜空間任務的強大實力。

The three choices many people make based on intuition all turned out to have hidden pitfalls in our testing. For instance, trying to save money by using Haiku 3.5 for multi-round coding: once it crosses a hidden threshold, it charges at five times the rate, and the resulting 3D effect is still subpar. If you want the best performance by maxing out the top-tier Opus 3.5 to the "Extra. Intelligence" level, you'll pay nearly 20%more across four tests, yet it didn't outperform the standard Opus at all. Even when using the new default setting for Opus 3.5, while it was the fastest of the bunch, it misidentified a simple speedometer chart in a test. Today, we’ll use four identical tests to help you navigate these six modes at once. Hi there, welcome back—this is the third installment of our full model series comparison. Today, we are. focusing on Anthropic’s current Claude lineup: Haiku 3.5, Sonnet 3.5, Opus 3.5 , and the Opus 3.5 (November 9th update ) series. Their output prices range from $ 0.50 all the way to $ 40, an 80-fold difference. Let’s jump straight into the first real-world test: asking these six modes to write a 3D off-road vehicle driving over an 18cm speed bump. This task.

requires running independently without a network, so I completely cut off the browser's external connection; tests showed all six modes had zero errors and ran successfully. Looking at this first round, the top-ranked Opus 3.5 took 44.7 minutes, costing $ 13.19 based on official API pricing. It produced a post-rain, blue-toned scene with clear puddle reflections on the wet ground, clean windows, and a. solid off-road chassis. We’ll turn on the audio to actually listen—the simulated engine and tire sound effects are the cleanest of the lot. Zooming the perspective into the wheel wells, you can see the thick axle connecting the left and right wheels and the gear assembly in the center. You can clearly see how the side-by-side red springs and yellow shock absorbers compress and move together. If you're used to seeing road cars where the spring is sleeved over the shock, you might think this was drawn incorrectly. That was my first impression too, but in fact, hardcore off-roaders like the Wrangler or the old Defender actually feature this factory-standard setup where the springs and shocks are mounted side-by-side. So, looking at it that way , it's actually quite an authentic reproduction. Let’s look at the main line S 5.5, which costs half as much as the top trim. place, Sea 5.5 H, took 31.9 minutes and 0.75 meters, making a Bumblebee with a black ball head and a capsule body, featuring only two brown flat wings with holes, lacking any rear wings or glass textures, remaining at the bottom. structure and three-dimensional breakdown, creating a two-layer hollow metal wing frame with blue gradient stained glass and gears sandwiched in between, and a clear metal color separation inside the open chest. When the yellow and red wheels turn, the dark gray metal rods follow, driving the wings to flap in a wide range. If we click the exploded view, we can even dismantle a single wing into four independent layers, though a few text labels get slightly crowded after. splitting, which is a small drawback. eye. Alright, after these two rounds, Phobol 5.2 has one win and one tie. The next third round will be the deciding match to determine the overall 3D victory. The third round tests long-text comprehension plus multi-step spatial assembly. We fed the model a 5-page English manual for wooden furniture assembly, requiring it to turn the 32 plywood parts into a set of 3D interactive assembly instructions, following the real hole positions and correct sequence. In this round, the gap between the high and low tiers has completely widened. Sixth place, Haiku.

5.5, ran for 31.6 minutes and cost $ 0.42; all the parts shrank into rough wooden strips, jammed together in a mess where you can't even see the wooden pegs entering the holes. At the final step, the tabletop stood 90 degrees in mid-air , causing the 3D model to collapse completely. Fifth place, S3 5.5 H, took 35 minutes and $ 4.41; all the way to the final step, the mismatched high and low table legs were still upside down, and the camera movements and page labels in the middle steps were also incorrect. . Both OPS 5.5 models held steady in the middle tier for this round, running through the entire process quite smoothly; fourth place, OPS 5.5 Medium, used 28.5 minutes and cost $ 4.48. It produced furniture and sanding animations, but it missed the grooves on the top of the middle layer boards. The opening labels were a bit off; third place, 5.5 H, used 29.3 minutes and $ 5.88, with the bilingual cards and real-time parts count clearly done, though the visual detail is simpler than. Phobol's. Moreover, in the very first second, the three-layer wooden boards were already stacked in advance, failing to start from the spread-out state as required. The tabletop also lacked the slots. Alright, the champion and runner-up were ultimately decided between the two Feibao 5.2 versions. The second-place Feibao 5.2 X took 40.6 minutes and cost $ 17.18. It aligned the contours of the 32 wooden boards very accurately, and even embedded the corresponding PDF manual illustration in the top right corner for easy reference . The final standing table was also quite sturdy. The only downside was the.

wooden dowel insertion step; the dowels stayed on the ground, then jumped directly into the holes in the next shot , missing the animation of them flying in. It also lacked the glue application and sanding animations. Meanwhile, the first-place Feibao 5.2 H took 45.4 minutes and cost $ 17.67. Not only did it align the contours and hole positions of the 32 boards most accurately, but it also broke the seven major steps down into 22 smooth processes. More importantly, it was the only one to show a clear, unobstructed close-up of all. sixteen 30mm and thirteen 25mm dowels flying into their holes one by one. It even included the entire woodworking process, from opening the glue bottle and applying glue along the boards, tightening six red-and-black clamps, sanding with sandpaper, to the color change of the wood after being brushed with oil. After testing all three medium-difficulty 3D puzzles, the Feibao 5.2 H secured a solid victory with two wins and one draw, while the more expensive Feibao 5.2 X failed to win a. single round. So, if we remove the complex 3D coding tasks and look at simple, static, daily-use image recognition questions, what surprises will these six models have in store? The fourth round consists of five objective questions based on static images. This quick-fire round includes identifying a Roman numeral clock set to 10:28, counting the number of eggs on a plate, recognizing the No. 28 tram in Lisbon, Portugal, spotting seven differences between two tomato photos, and accurately pinpointing the break in the.

# 第四关：看图快问五连

second line of Lincoln's handwritten letter. In this round, the 35.5 H took 11.1 minutes at a cost of $ 0.23, the OPS 5.5 H took 11.2 minutes at $ 0.49, and the Feibao 5.2 H took 11.5 minutes at $ 1.38. All three models cleanly achieved a perfect score of five points , with the SIT 5.5 being the most cost-effective among those with a perfect score. But two major discrepancies popped up immediately. The first was with the fastest model, o1 -mini, which took only 0.7 minutes (42. seconds) and cost $ 0.37, yet it misread the 10:28 on the clock as 10:32. This exceeded our two-minute tolerance, dropping it to fourth place. You should know that the official default for the s-series has always been 'High', but with o1-mini, this is the first time OpenAI has set the default reasoning effort to 'Medium'. If we calculate the total for these four questions, this change did allow o1- mini to achieve the fastest overall time of 62 minutes, and at $ 11.57, it was.

# 四道题合起来算：两个反差

only slightly more expensive than o1- preview. However, the trade-off is that it actually stumbled on visual judgment tasks, like reading clock hands. If we simply switch that same model to the ' High' setting for o1-mini, the total time for the four questions becomes 108 minutes at a cost of $ 17.63, which not only regains a perfect score on image tasks but also securely takes second and third place in the field car and wooden table questions. The second discrepancy appeared in the top-tier o1 5.2 x model. . Although it also achieved perfect scores on all five questions, it took a full 6.6 minutes just to look at these five static images. That's 4.4 times the time of o1-mini (High), and its hidden internal reasoning generated over 20,000 tokens. A simple visual question cost $ 3.66, which is 16 times that of o1-mini (High) for the same perfect score. As for Haiku 3.5 (High), it got three points in 10.1 minutes; it missed one spot in the tomato "find the difference " task, and for the handwritten Lincoln letter, it honestly admitted it couldn't. see it clearly. It only cost $ 0.02, but you have to watch out for those two cents, because out of all four questions in the set, only this one short task was involved. It didn't trigger the five-fold price hike hidden in the fine print of Haiku's pricing table. I went through the backend logs for these 24 tasks round by round, and once we looked at the price table, the real secret to the billing became completely clear. First, let's talk about the cheapest, Haiku 3.5. Many people look at the official OpenAI pricing table and only.

# 逐轮对账：Haiku 5.5 的 10 万 token 五倍涨价线

see $ 0.10 per million input tokens and $ 0.50 per output, with cache reads at $ 0.01. Thinking it's 20 times cheaper than the others, they use it for multi-round programming, assuming it's the most cost-effective—but the trap is hidden in the tier conditions below the table. While our four main models all provide a full million tokens of context , only Haiku 3.5 has a price-hike threshold at 100,000 tokens. As soon as a single-turn prompt context exceeds 100k, its input and output prices quintuple, becoming $ 0.50 per million for input and $ 2.50 for output. I. tracked all 100 request turns Haiku 3.5 made across the four tasks. Only the image-viewing task stayed under the limit, peaking at around 56,000 tokens. It kept its base price, but once you enter actual 3D coding, running checks and loops, the context quickly shatters that 100k barrier. For the wooden boat manual, over 80%of the turns exceeded this limit, while the moon rover reached as high as 94%, with a single-turn peak hitting 279,000. tokens. And for the mechanical butterfly , more than 96%of the text was billed at the 5x premium rate. If we estimate based on the surface-level low price under 100k, you might think these four tasks cost only $ 0.62. But if you calculate based on this tiered pricing, it jumps straight to $ 2.11. Total time was 86 minutes, the bill tripled to 3.4 x, and all you got in return was coming in last on all three 3D tasks. Next, let’s look at the most expensive tier— spending the most but winning nothing.

# 最贵那头：Fable XHigh 多花近两成，一题没赢过 High

After running all four tasks, Sonnet 3.5 H took 121 minutes for a total of $ 42.93, securing two wins and a draw in 3D, plus a perfect score in vision. Sonnet 3.5 X took 125 minutes for $ 51.03, costing over $ 8 more—nearly 19% pricier—yet it didn't win a single one of the four tasks against H. Taking just the mechanical butterfly task, X cost $ 9.07 more than H. Even when you place these two butterflies side-by-side, it’s still a draw, while it outright lost the. other two 3D tasks. This was proven with real money. We verified the honest truth in the official OpenAI documentation: most performance gains are already reached at the H tier; pushing further yields diminishing returns. Alright, let’s wrap up with the three core findings from today’s tests. First, Haiku 3.5 will cross the 100,000-token red line by a large margin as soon as it enters multi-turn long-form coding. The unit price will jump fivefold, and complex 3D tasks will lead to a total performance collapse. Second, the top-tier Sonnet 3.5 H is more than.

enough. Pushing to the X tier costs nearly 20%more, yet it didn’t win a single one of the four tasks. Third, the official default for OPS 5.5 has been lowered to medium, offering the shortest total runtime, but for detailed tasks and heavy engineering, I still recommend manual adjustment to a higher tier. So, how should we choose in our daily work? Just look at the task at hand. For short text classification, information extraction, or tasks under 100,000 tokens per round, you can use Flash 5.5 ; it’s the most cost-effective. For daily tasks like image analysis,.

# 按手上的活怎么选

document Q&A, or lightweight development , choose SIT 5.5 H; it gets a perfect score on image tasks. If your main focus is writing code or building prototypes quickly, use the new default OPS 5.5 medium; it's just slightly more expensive than the former. When dealing with high-precision recognition or heavy engineering, manually switch to OPS 5.5 High; it can break into the top three at half the price of the flagship model. But if you really need to go for top-tier results and complex project deployment, just use 5.2 H directly. As. for X, unless you have tested and seen a clear improvement in your own ultra-long tasks, there is no need to enable it for routine work. I’ve packed the 18 interactive 3D final products from this run into an online exhibit. The link is in the video description; feel free to check it out yourself. Especially in the mechanical butterfly section, carefully compare Flash High and FBX, then tell me in the comments which one you think is better. Alright, that’s all for this sharing. I’m XON, see you in the next one.

摘要

模型選擇的迷思與實測背景

作者指出，許多人在面對 Anthropic 的 Claude 系列模型及思考預算切換開關時，往往會依照直覺挑選，但這些選擇背後卻暗藏成本翻倍或性能不符預期的陷阱。例如使用輕量級模型進行多輪編程時可能觸發高倍費率，或開啟最高智慧等級卻多付了將近兩成費用且未帶來明顯效益。為了釐清真相，作者針對多種配置與模式展開了相同條件下的橫向評測，從生成品質、耗費時間與API 成本進行深度剖析。

第一輪測試：3D 越野車越障模擬

第一項挑戰要求模型在完全斷網的環境下，撰寫出能夠翻越 18 公分減速帶的3D 越野車動力模擬。雖然所有配置皆成功運行，但在細節呈現上差距甚大。高階配置成功還原了雨後地面積水倒影、乾淨車窗以及與實車相同的並列彈簧避震結構；官方預設模式則以最快速度與適中成本取得極佳平衡。相對地，低階模型不僅材質簡陋，甚至出現了煞車卡鉗隨輪胎轉動的荒謬機械錯誤。

第二輪測試：精細機械蝴蝶與展開視圖

第二項測試聚焦於多層微型零件聯動，要求模型打造出兼具金屬鏤空、彩繪玻璃與胸腔齒輪聯動的互動式 3D 機械蝴蝶，並支援一鍵爆炸圖拆解。在此測試中，中低階模型紛紛暴露出過曝、透明度欠佳或結構如玩具般的缺陷。兩款頂級配置在細節與節奏感上難分伯仲，但作者特別指出，開啟最高思考預算的模式耗時與費用足足翻倍，肉眼可見的成果卻無實質差距。

第三輪測試：長文本空間組裝導引

第三輪任務考驗長文本理解與空間幾何組裝，模型需依據五頁英文家具手冊，將 32 個板材零件按孔位和順序轉化為互動組裝流程。這項測試徹底拉開了高低階之間的差距：低階模型組裝邏輯完全崩潰、桌面漂浮空中；中階模型能流暢運行卻遺漏了凹槽等細部特徵；唯有頂規配置能精準定位零件輪廓並嵌入手冊圖解，展現出處理複雜空間任務的強大實力。

requires running independently without a network, so I completely cut off the browser's external connection; tests showed all six modes had zero errors and ran successfully. That was my first impression too, but in fact, hardcore off-roaders like the Wrangler or the old Defender actually feature this factory-standard setup where the springs and shocks are mounted side-by-side. So, looking at it that way , it's actually quite an authentic reproduction. Let’s look at the main line S 5.5, which costs half as much as the top trim. minutes at a cost of $ 6.16 to take second place. It includes millimeter annotations that bounce along with the suspension, and the mechanical movement is up to par. cohesive vibe? If we switch to a challenge that specifically requires interlocking multiple layers of fine parts, can the F 5.2 make a comeback with all those extra details? place, Sea 5.5 H, took 31.9 minutes and 0.75 meters, making a Bumblebee with a black ball head and a capsule body, featuring only two brown flat wings with holes, lacking any rear wings or glass textures, remaining at the bottom. To be honest, I've looked at these two versions back and forth several times, and I really can't tell by eye which one is definitively better, because they each win on completely different details . The 5.2 H wins on its true hollow.

structure and three-dimensional breakdown, creating a two-layer hollow metal wing frame with blue gradient stained glass and gears sandwiched in between, and a clear metal color separation inside the open chest. When the yellow and red wheels turn, the dark gray metal rods follow, driving the wings to flap in a wide range. If we click the exploded view, we can even dismantle a single wing into four independent layers, though a few text labels get slightly crowded after. splitting, which is a small drawback. The 5.2 X wins on insect detailing and dynamic rhythm, creating six thin, multi-jointed yellow legs. Faceted emerald compound eyes and glowing ruby-like antennae. When they flap front and back, there's a staggered rhythmic sense to it, like a living creature. If we click the exploded view, it automatically slows down the deletion speed, accompanied by bilingual instructions on the left and right. So, for this round, my most honest judgment is to call it a draw between the two. eye. Alright, after these two rounds, Phobol 5.2 has one win and one tie. The next third round will be the deciding match to determine the overall 3D victory. At the final step, the tabletop stood 90 degrees in mid-air , causing the 3D model to collapse completely. The opening labels were a bit off; third place, 5.5 H, used 29.3 minutes and $ 5.88, with the bilingual cards and real-time parts count clearly done, though the visual detail is simpler than. The tabletop also lacked the slots. Alright, the champion and runner-up were ultimately decided between the two Feibao 5.2 versions. The second-place Feibao 5.2 X took 40.6 minutes and cost $ 17.18. wooden dowel insertion step; the dowels stayed on the ground, then jumped directly into the holes in the next shot , missing the animation of them flying in. Not only did it align the contours and hole positions of the 32 boards most accurately, but it also broke the seven major steps down into 22 smooth processes. More importantly, it was the only one to show a clear, unobstructed close-up of all. sixteen 30mm and thirteen 25mm dowels flying into their holes one by one. It even included the entire woodworking process, from opening the glue bottle and applying glue along the boards, tightening six red-and-black clamps, sanding with sandpaper, to the color change of the wood after being brushed with oil. After testing all three medium-difficulty 3D puzzles, the Feibao 5.2 H secured a solid victory with two wins and one draw, while the more expensive Feibao 5.2 X failed to win a. single round. So, if we remove the complex 3D coding tasks and look at simple, static, daily-use image recognition questions, what surprises will these six models have in store? The fourth round consists of five objective questions based on static images. This quick-fire round includes identifying a Roman numeral clock set to 10:28, counting the number of eggs on a plate, recognizing the No. 28 tram in Lisbon, Portugal, spotting seven differences between two tomato photos, and accurately pinpointing the break in the.

second line of Lincoln's handwritten letter. You should know that the official default for the s-series has always been 'High', but with o1-mini, this is the first time OpenAI has set the default reasoning effort to 'Medium'. If we calculate the total for these four questions, this change did allow o1- mini to achieve the fastest overall time of 62 minutes, and at $ 11.57, it was.

only slightly more expensive than o1- preview. However, the trade-off is that it actually stumbled on visual judgment tasks, like reading clock hands. If we simply switch that same model to the ' High' setting for o1-mini, the total time for the four questions becomes 108 minutes at a cost of $ 17.63, which not only regains a perfect score on image tasks but also securely takes second and third place in the field car and wooden table questions. The second discrepancy appeared in the top-tier o1 5.2 x model. . Although it also achieved perfect scores on all five questions, it took a full 6.6 minutes just to look at these five static images. I went through the backend logs for these 24 tasks round by round, and once we looked at the price table, the real secret to the billing became completely clear. First, let's talk about the cheapest, Haiku 3.5. Many people look at the official OpenAI pricing table and only.

# 逐轮对账：Haiku 5.5 的 10 万 token 五倍涨价线

see $ 0.10 per million input tokens and $ 0.50 per output, with cache reads at $ 0.01. Thinking it's 20 times cheaper than the others, they use it for multi-round programming, assuming it's the most cost-effective—but the trap is hidden in the tier conditions below the table. While our four main models all provide a full million tokens of context , only Haiku 3.5 has a price-hike threshold at 100,000 tokens. As soon as a single-turn prompt context exceeds 100k, its input and output prices quintuple, becoming $ 0.50 per million for input and $ 2.50 for output. I. tracked all 100 request turns Haiku 3.5 made across the four tasks. Only the image-viewing task stayed under the limit, peaking at around 56,000 tokens. It kept its base price, but once you enter actual 3D coding, running checks and loops, the context quickly shatters that 100k barrier. For the wooden boat manual, over 80%of the turns exceeded this limit, while the moon rover reached as high as 94%, with a single-turn peak hitting 279,000. tokens. And for the mechanical butterfly , more than 96%of the text was billed at the 5x premium rate. If we estimate based on the surface-level low price under 100k, you might think these four tasks cost only $ 0.62. But if you calculate based on this tiered pricing, it jumps straight to $ 2.11. Total time was 86 minutes, the bill tripled to 3.4 x, and all you got in return was coming in last on all three 3D tasks. Next, let’s look at the most expensive tier— spending the most but winning nothing.

# 最贵那头：Fable XHigh 多花近两成，一题没赢过 High

After running all four tasks, Sonnet 3.5 H took 121 minutes for a total of $ 42.93, securing two wins and a draw in 3D, plus a perfect score in vision. Taking just the mechanical butterfly task, X cost $ 9.07 more than H. Even when you place these two butterflies side-by-side, it’s still a draw, while it outright lost the. other two 3D tasks. This was proven with real money. We verified the honest truth in the official OpenAI documentation: most performance gains are already reached at the H tier; pushing further yields diminishing returns. Alright, let’s wrap up with the three core findings from today’s tests. First, Haiku 3.5 will cross the 100,000-token red line by a large margin as soon as it enters multi-turn long-form coding. The unit price will jump fivefold, and complex 3D tasks will lead to a total performance collapse. Second, the top-tier Sonnet 3.5 H is more than.

# 三个核心发现

enough. Pushing to the X tier costs nearly 20%more, yet it didn’t win a single one of the four tasks. Third, the official default for OPS 5.5 has been lowered to medium, offering the shortest total runtime, but for detailed tasks and heavy engineering, I still recommend manual adjustment to a higher tier. So, how should we choose in our daily work? Just look at the task at hand. For short text classification, information extraction, or tasks under 100,000 tokens per round, you can use Flash 5.5 ; it’s the most cost-effective. For daily tasks like image analysis,.

document Q&A, or lightweight development , choose SIT 5.5 H; it gets a perfect score on image tasks. But if you really need to go for top-tier results and complex project deployment, just use 5.2 H directly. As. for X, unless you have tested and seen a clear improvement in your own ultra-long tasks, there is no need to enable it for routine work. 摘要

模型選擇的迷思與實測背景

作者指出，許多人在面對 Anthropic 的 Claude 系列模型及思考預算切換開關時，往往會依照直覺挑選，但這些選擇背後卻暗藏成本翻倍或性能不符預期的陷阱。例如使用輕量級模型進行多輪編程時可能觸發高倍費率，或開啟最高智慧等級卻多付了將近兩成費用且未帶來明顯效益。為了釐清真相，作者針對多種配置與模式展開了相同條件下的橫向評測，從生成品質、耗費時間與API 成本進行深度剖析。

第一輪測試：3D 越野車越障模擬

第一項挑戰要求模型在完全斷網的環境下，撰寫出能夠翻越 18 公分減速帶的3D 越野車動力模擬。雖然所有配置皆成功運行，但在細節呈現上差距甚大。高階配置成功還原了雨後地面積水倒影、乾淨車窗以及與實車相同的並列彈簧避震結構；官方預設模式則以最快速度與適中成本取得極佳平衡。相對地，低階模型不僅材質簡陋，甚至出現了煞車卡鉗隨輪胎轉動的荒謬機械錯誤。

第二輪測試：精細機械蝴蝶與展開視圖

第二項測試聚焦於多層微型零件聯動，要求模型打造出兼具金屬鏤空、彩繪玻璃與胸腔齒輪聯動的互動式 3D 機械蝴蝶，並支援一鍵爆炸圖拆解。在此測試中，中低階模型紛紛暴露出過曝、透明度欠佳或結構如玩具般的缺陷。兩款頂級配置在細節與節奏感上難分伯仲，但作者特別指出，開啟最高思考預算的模式耗時與費用足足翻倍，肉眼可見的成果卻無實質差距。

第三輪測試：長文本空間組裝導引

第三輪任務考驗長文本理解與空間幾何組裝，模型需依據五頁英文家具手冊，將 32 個板材零件按孔位和順序轉化為互動組裝流程。這項測試徹底拉開了高低階之間的差距：低階模型組裝邏輯完全崩潰、桌面漂浮空中；中階模型能流暢運行卻遺漏了凹槽等細部特徵；唯有頂規配置能精準定位零件輪廓並嵌入手冊圖解，展現出處理複雜空間任務的強大實力。

Intelligence" level, you'll pay nearly 20%more across four tests, yet it didn't outperform the standard Opus at all. That was my first impression too, but in fact, hardcore off-roaders like the Wrangler or the old Defender actually feature this factory-standard setup where the springs and shocks are mounted side-by-side. minutes at a cost of $ 6.16 to take second place. It includes millimeter annotations that bounce along with the suspension, and the mechanical movement is up to par. cohesive vibe? If we switch to a challenge that specifically requires interlocking multiple layers of fine parts, can the F 5.2 make a comeback with all those extra details? place, Sea 5.5 H, took 31.9 minutes and 0.75 meters, making a Bumblebee with a black ball head and a capsule body, featuring only two brown flat wings with holes, lacking any rear wings or glass textures, remaining at the bottom. To be honest, I've looked at these two versions back and forth several times, and I really can't tell by eye which one is definitively better, because they each win on completely different details . The 5.2 H wins on its true hollow.

structure and three-dimensional breakdown, creating a two-layer hollow metal wing frame with blue gradient stained glass and gears sandwiched in between, and a clear metal color separation inside the open chest. When the yellow and red wheels turn, the dark gray metal rods follow, driving the wings to flap in a wide range. If we click the exploded view, we can even dismantle a single wing into four independent layers, though a few text labels get slightly crowded after. splitting, which is a small drawback. The 5.2 X wins on insect detailing and dynamic rhythm, creating six thin, multi-jointed yellow legs. Faceted emerald compound eyes and glowing ruby-like antennae. When they flap front and back, there's a staggered rhythmic sense to it, like a living creature. If we click the exploded view, it automatically slows down the deletion speed, accompanied by bilingual instructions on the left and right. However, when it expands, it's vertical. , with almost no spacing, and the left instruction panel occasionally has two minor instances of overlapping text; these are just minor flaws. So, for this round, my most honest judgment is to call it a draw between the two. But if we consider the time and cost for a side-by-side comparison, the same Phobol 5.2 model running on Xi took nearly twice as long and cost nearly twice as much, $ 19.77 versus $ 10.70, with no visible difference to the naked.

eye. Alright, after these two rounds, Phobol 5.2 has one win and one tie. The next third round will be the deciding match to determine the overall 3D victory. The third round tests long-text comprehension plus multi-step spatial assembly. We fed the model a 5-page English manual for wooden furniture assembly, requiring it to turn the 32 plywood parts into a set of 3D interactive assembly instructions, following the real hole positions and correct sequence. 5.5, ran for 31.6 minutes and cost $ 0.42; all the parts shrank into rough wooden strips, jammed together in a mess where you can't even see the wooden pegs entering the holes. At the final step, the tabletop stood 90 degrees in mid-air , causing the 3D model to collapse completely. The opening labels were a bit off; third place, 5.5 H, used 29.3 minutes and $ 5.88, with the bilingual cards and real-time parts count clearly done, though the visual detail is simpler than. wooden dowel insertion step; the dowels stayed on the ground, then jumped directly into the holes in the next shot , missing the animation of them flying in. second line of Lincoln's handwritten letter. If we calculate the total for these four questions, this change did allow o1- mini to achieve the fastest overall time of 62 minutes, and at $ 11.57, it was.

only slightly more expensive than o1- preview. However, the trade-off is that it actually stumbled on visual judgment tasks, like reading clock hands. The second discrepancy appeared in the top-tier o1 5.2 x model. . Although it also achieved perfect scores on all five questions, it took a full 6.6 minutes just to look at these five static images. First, let's talk about the cheapest, Haiku 3.5. Many people look at the official OpenAI pricing table and only.

# 逐轮对账：Haiku 5.5 的 10 万 token 五倍涨价线

see $ 0.10 per million input tokens and $ 0.50 per output, with cache reads at $ 0.01. Thinking it's 20 times cheaper than the others, they use it for multi-round programming, assuming it's the most cost-effective—but the trap is hidden in the tier conditions below the table. While our four main models all provide a full million tokens of context , only Haiku 3.5 has a price-hike threshold at 100,000 tokens. As soon as a single-turn prompt context exceeds 100k, its input and output prices quintuple, becoming $ 0.50 per million for input and $ 2.50 for output. I. tracked all 100 request turns Haiku 3.5 made across the four tasks. Only the image-viewing task stayed under the limit, peaking at around 56,000 tokens. And for the mechanical butterfly , more than 96%of the text was billed at the 5x premium rate. If we estimate based on the surface-level low price under 100k, you might think these four tasks cost only $ 0.62. But if you calculate based on this tiered pricing, it jumps straight to $ 2.11. Total time was 86 minutes, the bill tripled to 3.4 x, and all you got in return was coming in last on all three 3D tasks. Next, let’s look at the most expensive tier— spending the most but winning nothing.

# 最贵那头：Fable XHigh 多花近两成，一题没赢过 High

After running all four tasks, Sonnet 3.5 H took 121 minutes for a total of $ 42.93, securing two wins and a draw in 3D, plus a perfect score in vision. This was proven with real money. We verified the honest truth in the official OpenAI documentation: most performance gains are already reached at the H tier; pushing further yields diminishing returns. Alright, let’s wrap up with the three core findings from today’s tests. First, Haiku 3.5 will cross the 100,000-token red line by a large margin as soon as it enters multi-turn long-form coding. The unit price will jump fivefold, and complex 3D tasks will lead to a total performance collapse. Second, the top-tier Sonnet 3.5 H is more than.

enough. Pushing to the X tier costs nearly 20%more, yet it didn’t win a single one of the four tasks. Third, the official default for OPS 5.5 has been lowered to medium, offering the shortest total runtime, but for detailed tasks and heavy engineering, I still recommend manual adjustment to a higher tier. So, how should we choose in our daily work? Just look at the task at hand. For short text classification, information extraction, or tasks under 100,000 tokens per round, you can use Flash 5.5 ; it’s the most cost-effective. For daily tasks like image analysis,.

document Q&A, or lightweight development , choose SIT 5.5 H; it gets a perfect score on image tasks. But if you really need to go for top-tier results and complex project deployment, just use 5.2 H directly. As. for X, unless you have tested and seen a clear improvement in your own ultra-long tasks, there is no need to enable it for routine work. 摘要

月球車懸吊模擬：細節決定成敗的旗艦對決

作者針對 OpenAI 推出的 GPT-6 系列六個層級展開深度測試，首項任務要求模型編寫一套可離線運行的 3D 越野月球車模擬程式，並具備避震特寫與慢動作功能。入門的 Luna 與 Tera 雖然運行迅速且成本極低，但生成的車輛僅如積木方塊，避震彈簧甚至完全錯位；中階的 Smedium 與 SX 雖然外觀進步，卻分別出現輪胎穿模與避震頂座穿透車身的嚴重複陷。進入旗艦對決，單線程的 AstraHigh 耗時 21.2 分鐘，外觀氛圍優良，但拉近檢視卻發現彈簧內部全空、缺乏阻尼桿；而能夠自動指派多子代理的 AstraUltra 則完整構建出黑色避震筒、銀色伸縮桿與六角螺絲底座，甚至提供了車輪內部視角切換功能，以扎實的結構細節拔得頭籌，取得 1 比 0 領先。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入解析 Google 在 36 天內密集推出的四款 Gemini 系列模型（Argon、Carbon、Hydrogen、Near）的底層技術血脈與定位差異。
  • 透過耗時逾十小時的實測揭露「預設模式」的嚴重缺陷，並證實開啟深度推理模式如何讓模型輸出品質產生脫胎換骨的飛躍。
  • 對比單一模型與多模型協同工作（Orchestrator）在 3D 物理模擬、精細機械渲染與工程文件動畫化中的實際效能與成本差異。

摘要

模型血統解析與預設模式的陷阱

作者指出，Google 在短短 36 天內接連推出宛如元素週期表命名的四款模型，令許多使用者摸不著頭緒。透過查閱官方技術文檔，作者釐清了這條家族血緣：最早發布的 Argon 是純粹的混合專家架構（MoE）底模，而隨後的 Carbon 則針對深度推理進行強化，至於 Hydrogen 與 Near 皆是由 Carbon 分支演化而來。目前 Google 官方已在推薦清單中以 Near 取代 Argon，甚至在 AI Studio 的下拉選單中將其設為預設首選。然而，作者實測發現，官方榜單上號稱超越 Carbon 的高分，必須在手動開啟最高推理模式下才能實現；若僅依賴選單頂端的預設狀態，模型在多項複雜實測中的表現反而墊底。

極限實測：3D 物理模擬與精密機械結構

在作者設計的「越野車減速帶 3D 物理挑戰」中，測試重點在於輪胎貼地性、避震彈簧壓縮回彈以及車身動態姿態。開啟最高推理的頂級模型耗時約 24.7 分鐘，精準模擬出消光橄欖綠車漆、輪拱陰影與黃金避震器細節，展現如汽車廣告般的動態光影；反觀頂端預設模式不僅視角呆板且排氣管高光過曝，甚至排在第四名。更令人驚豔的是，採取多模型協同架構（Orchestrator）的組合僅花費 19.6 分鐘便奪下第三名，速度冠絕全場。在隨後的「3D 互動機械蝴蝶」試驗中，Carbon 開啟高推理模式以 30.7 分鐘拿下冠軍，完美渲染鈦金屬、香檳金齒輪咬合與四層爆炸圖；而關閉推理的預設模式產生的翅膀卻退化為死板的太陽能板狀網格，甚至發生主齒輪穿模的嚴重瑕疵，證明在複雜 3D 機械編程中，是否開啟深度推理決定了成品的成敗。

複雜手冊動態化與多模型協同架構優勢

為了進一步驗證預設模式的短板，作者測試將五頁 PDF 書桌組裝說明書轉換為「3D 步驟拆解動畫」。在此極限挑戰中，開啟最高推理的 Near 耗時 49.8 分鐘，精準捕捉對稱錯位桌腿與百個孔洞木榫安裝動畫；而預設模式不僅算錯零件數量，動畫更卡死在靜態爆炸圖上，再次印證面對重度工程任務時切忌使用預設狀態。相對地，在羅馬競技場識別、找不同等五項快速靜態視覺問答中，輕量化 Flash 模式僅用 1.6 分鐘與 0.19 美元即全數通關，性價比極高。作者總結，靜態影像分析無法拉開模型差距，真正的分水嶺在於推理深度；而 Google 的多模型協同架構自動由主力模型統籌拆解任務、調度廉價輕量模型平行編寫子模組，在各項嚴苛測試中展現出壓制單一模型的強大競爭力。

================================================

# 开场：10 小时实测反常结果

The lunar rover in this video, featuring realistic spring compression, along with this four-layer mechanical butterfly, were both created by Google's new Gemini 1.5. In just over a month, they’ve densely released four different models, with names that feel like the periodic table, making it easy to get confused. To help you fully understand the true characteristics of these four models in the Gemini family, I spent over ten hours running side-by-side tests on six different versions using the same set of. questions, and the results were quite unusual. The default version that Google places at the top of the menu actually ranked last in the tests, even missing a piece of the instruction manual's animation. However, just by toggling one setting, it immediately surpassed the top-tier Carbon model to take first place; even more surprisingly, in the second half, we tested Google's official multi-model orchestration. That is the " Orchestrator," where we had Near team up with Hydrogen to tackle the tasks. For all three major questions, it won 3-0,. beating out any single model. It even produced the best result for the lunar rover test; hey there, welcome back, Google released Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen , and Near in just 36 days. Even I was initially confused about these four models: were they really trained on different base architectures ? Or, as rumors online suggest, are they just lightweight versions modified from the others? We opened the official technical cards for all four DeepMind models, and the.

# 拆穿 Gemini 4 血缘与价格倒挂

truth boils down to a single line of lineage: the Argon released on October 13th is the original Mixture-of-Experts base for the entire family. It was not created by fine-tuning an older model. The Carbon released on November 10th is optimized for deep reasoning, while Hydrogen on November 12th and Near on November 18th were all branched out from the top-tier Carbon; so, where did the earliest release, Argon, go? In the family chart on the official November 18th blog post, Argon. has already been removed, leaving only Carbon, Hydrogen, and Near. The Gemini app menu for regular users has also been replaced by Near. Opening Google's own AI engineering tool , AI Studio, the top of the drop-down menu is now the default Near, followed by the four single models and the Orchestrator, with the official blog citing a third-party leaderboard claiming Near scored 61 points, surpassing Carbon's 60. Many people think they can just use the. default model, but you haven't noticed that the score that surpassed the rest was actually achieved by turning on the highest "reasoning" mode. Before the end of the month, there's a price inversion ; they are all priced similarly around the million-token mark. When hitting the cache, the retrieval cost is only 5%of a standard input, but the top-tier Claude is still in its promotional period until November 30th; its API unit price is about two-thirds of the new Opus model, only rising to the full price on December 1st. So, with the unit price being one-third cheaper right now, is the total cost for the entire run really. more economical? Let's head straight to the testing site. The first task is our brand new offline 3D physics challenge: have these six models write code to build an off-road vehicle driving over a speed bump. We are focusing on three physical details: when the front wheels hit the speed bump, can the tires stay in contact with the ground throughout? How do the springs and shock absorbers compress and rebound relative to the chassis? And when does the car body slowly lift following the motion? All six models successfully executed the suspension compression, but you can tell.

# 实测 1：越野车过减速坎

the difference in quality at a glance. Ranking first is the Claude Opus model with "highest reasoning" enabled, taking 24.7 minutes—over ten minutes faster than the top-tier Claude. a 3D step-by-step assembly animation. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入解析 Google 在 36 天內密集推出的四款 Gemini 系列模型（Argon、Carbon、Hydrogen、Near）的底層技術血脈與定位差異。
  • 透過耗時逾十小時的實測揭露「預設模式」的嚴重缺陷，並證實開啟深度推理模式如何讓模型輸出品質產生脫胎換骨的飛躍。
  • 對比單一模型與多模型協同工作（Orchestrator）在 3D 物理模擬、精細機械渲染與工程文件動畫化中的實際效能與成本差異。

摘要

模型血統解析與預設模式的陷阱

作者指出，Google 在短短 36 天內接連推出宛如元素週期表命名的四款模型，令許多使用者摸不著頭緒。透過查閱官方技術文檔，作者釐清了這條家族血緣：最早發布的 Argon 是純粹的混合專家架構（MoE）底模，而隨後的 Carbon 則針對深度推理進行強化，至於 Hydrogen 與 Near 皆是由 Carbon 分支演化而來。目前 Google 官方已在推薦清單中以 Near 取代 Argon，甚至在 AI Studio 的下拉選單中將其設為預設首選。然而，作者實測發現，官方榜單上號稱超越 Carbon 的高分，必須在手動開啟最高推理模式下才能實現；若僅依賴選單頂端的預設狀態，模型在多項複雜實測中的表現反而墊底。

極限實測：3D 物理模擬與精密機械結構

在作者設計的「越野車減速帶 3D 物理挑戰」中，測試重點在於輪胎貼地性、避震彈簧壓縮回彈以及車身動態姿態。開啟最高推理的頂級模型耗時約 24.7 分鐘，精準模擬出消光橄欖綠車漆、輪拱陰影與黃金避震器細節，展現如汽車廣告般的動態光影；反觀頂端預設模式不僅視角呆板且排氣管高光過曝，甚至排在第四名。更令人驚豔的是，採取多模型協同架構（Orchestrator）的組合僅花費 19.6 分鐘便奪下第三名，速度冠絕全場。在隨後的「3D 互動機械蝴蝶」試驗中，Carbon 開啟高推理模式以 30.7 分鐘拿下冠軍，完美渲染鈦金屬、香檳金齒輪咬合與四層爆炸圖；而關閉推理的預設模式產生的翅膀卻退化為死板的太陽能板狀網格，甚至發生主齒輪穿模的嚴重瑕疵，證明在複雜 3D 機械編程中，是否開啟深度推理決定了成品的成敗。

複雜手冊動態化與多模型協同架構優勢

為了進一步驗證預設模式的短板，作者測試將五頁 PDF 書桌組裝說明書轉換為「3D 步驟拆解動畫」。在此極限挑戰中，開啟最高推理的 Near 耗時 49.8 分鐘，精準捕捉對稱錯位桌腿與百個孔洞木榫安裝動畫；而預設模式不僅算錯零件數量，動畫更卡死在靜態爆炸圖上，再次印證面對重度工程任務時切忌使用預設狀態。相對地，在羅馬競技場識別、找不同等五項快速靜態視覺問答中，輕量化 Flash 模式僅用 1.6 分鐘與 0.19 美元即全數通關，性價比極高。作者總結，靜態影像分析無法拉開模型差距，真正的分水嶺在於推理深度；而 Google 的多模型協同架構自動由主力模型統籌拆解任務、調度廉價輕量模型平行編寫子模組，在各項嚴苛測試中展現出壓制單一模型的強大競爭力。
